name_note: The GTDB genus Faucicola holds genomes that NCBI labels Moraxella or Enhydrobacter, matching a published reclassification of several Moraxella species into Faucicola.

sentences.text: Faucicola is a genus of Gram-negative bacteria in the family Moraxellaceae; a taxogenomic study reassigned Moraxella boevrei, Moraxella osloensis and Moraxella atlantae to this genus.
Faucicola mancuniensis has been isolated from the human respiratory tract, and a genomic study of one isolate reported a 2,740,046 bp genome that was susceptible to all 29 antibiotics tested.
Moraxella osloensis, one of the species reassigned to Faucicola, has been isolated from human skin and was described as an abundant skin bacterium in a single-cell sequencing study.
A skin metagenomic study identified Moraxella osloensis as a species specific for Chinese skin and as the signature species of one of two microbial network patterns, or cutotypes.
The wider genus Moraxella, from which these species come, has been described as inhabiting human and animal mucosa as well as water, soil and food.
